pathway.title: DXP ENTERPRISES INC — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Earnings are broad and growing, which is the main support for debt service. Twelve-month sales were USD 2,212.7 million, up 9.74% on FY2025, and reported EBITDA rose 13.07% to USD 247.2 million, lifting the margin from 10.84% to 11.17%; no customer reached 10% of sales and organic sales rose 9.26% in nine months 2026. Basis: calculation B01; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

Leverage is moderate but has drifted up because growth is paid for with cash. Net debt rose 15.50% to USD 604.4 million while twelve-month EBITDA rose 13.07%, so net leverage moved from 2.39x at 2025-12-31 to 2.45x and total leverage is 3.33x; the company's own secured leverage of 2.30x is lower because it uses principal debt and covenant EBITDA of USD 270.0 million. These figures are before the acquisition agreed on 2026-11-01 and the new buyback; pro forma net debt and leverage are not established, because the price and any purchase are not stated. Basis: calculation B02; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 2

Debt service is covered with room. Cash interest cover is 4.20x, liquidity is 48.47x the USD 8.5 million of principal due each year to 2029, and each 100 bp on the floating-rate term loan costs about USD 8.4 million, or 3.40% of EBITDA; with no hedges in place, a 200 bp rise would cut cover to 3.27x if the whole balance floats. Basis: calculation B03; calculation B04; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

Refinancing risk is concentrated in one year. USD 812.0 million, 96.72% of principal and 3.28x EBITDA, falls due on 2030-10-13, while the revolver now runs to 2031-07-02; S&P raised the rating to B+ in July 2026 and Moody's rated the corporate credit B1 at the end of 2025, but no market quotes are supplied, so pricing and market access are not established. Basis: calculation B05; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

Free cash flow is positive but flattered, so growth is not self-funded. Twelve-month free cash flow of USD 105.0 million compares with USD 54.0 million in FY2025 and benefits from cash taxes of USD 6.6 million against USD 35.1 million and capital expenditure of USD 10.2 million against USD 37.0 million in nine months; after USD 126.2 million of cash acquisitions the nine-month figure was negative USD 55.7 million, and free cash flow covered only 58.52% of cash acquisitions from 2024 to nine months 2026. Basis: calculation B06; calculation B07; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

Gross margin is the pressure point: it fell each quarter of 2026, from 32.3% to 31.8% to 30.7%, and the third quarter was 0.70 percentage points below a year earlier, which the company ties to higher input costs. Operating leverage hid this, because selling, general and administrative expense fell to 21.81% of third-quarter sales from 22.88%, but a further 100 bp of EBITDA margin loss would cost USD 22.1 million, 8.95% of EBITDA, and lift net leverage to 2.69x on unchanged net debt. Basis: calculation B09; 10-Q_2026-03-31_dxpe-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dxpe-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

Financial policy is the swing factor for creditors. The company pays no common dividend and bought no shares in nine months 2026, but it authorized a USD 150.0 million buyback on 2026-10-28, equal to 142.91% of twelve-month free cash flow, while its chief executive's holding and the board's independence are not established; Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk as Medium. Basis: calculation B10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

Business risk is moderate. Service Centers supply 64.23% of nine-month 2026 sales and depend on manufacturers who can cancel authorizations on little notice, part of revenue follows oil, gas and petrochemical spending, and tariffs and vendor price increases press on margin; against that, water and wastewater pumping now supplies 24.06% of sales at a 17.70% operating margin, with USD 325.0 million of backlog at the end of 2025. Basis: calculation B08; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24

cells.text: DXP Enterprises, Inc., a Texas corporation listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market (DXPE), headquartered in Houston, Texas

Business-to-business distributor of maintenance, repair and operating (MRO) products and services to industrial customers, with engineered pump packages, pump remanufacturing and outsourced supply chain management; founded in 1908

United States (96.18% of 2025 sales) and Canada (3.72%); 293 locations at 2025-12-31 in 39 U.S. states, nine Canadian provinces and one city each in the United Arab Emirates, India and Saudi Arabia; operations also in Mexico
Industrial distribution; the market is highly fragmented and DXP was the 17th largest U.S. distributor of MRO products on 2024 sales
Service Centers USD 1,373.140 million (68.10%); Innovative Pumping Solutions USD 390.291 million (19.36%); Supply Chain Services USD 252.934 million (12.54%); total USD 2,016.365 million
Service Centers USD 1,082.511 million (64.23%); Innovative Pumping Solutions USD 405.514 million (24.06%); Supply Chain Services USD 197.274 million (11.71%); total USD 1,685.299 million

Service Centers sell more than 1,000,000 items as a first-tier distributor from branches with same-day delivery; Innovative Pumping Solutions engineers and fabricates custom pump packages, remanufactures pumps and serves water and wastewater markets; Supply Chain Services runs customers' procurement and storerooms under long-term contracts that can be cancelled on little or no notice

No customer reached 10% of revenues in the last three fiscal years; over 90% of sales are products and under 10% are services; DXP traditionally has no long-term customer contracts outside Supply Chain Services

First-tier distributor buying from manufacturers; distribution authorizations can be cancelled, some on little or no notice; management language: it represents manufacturers of up to 90% of customers' MRO products
3,286 at 2025-12-31, of whom 3,038 in the United States; no U.S. employee is represented by a union
64 acquisitions since 2004; six in 2025 for USD 79.2 million and five in nine months 2026 for USD 153.6 million; management language: acquisitions are a key component of the growth strategy

runs.text: Strength: customer breadth supports revenue durability. No customer reached 10% of sales in three years, over 90% of sales are products, and organic sales rose 9.26% in nine months 2026, so the earnings that service debt do not rest on one account or on acquisitions alone. Basis: calculation B01; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

Strength: liquidity and a light amortization profile remove near-term cash risk. Liquidity of USD 411.0 million is 48.47x the USD 8.5 million of principal due each year to 2029, and the revolver was extended to 2031-07-02. Basis: calculation B03; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

Strength: coverage and margin trajectory are favorable. Cash interest cover is 4.20x and the EBITDA margin rose from 10.84% in FY2025 to 11.17% over twelve months, helped by selling, general and administrative leverage. Basis: calculation B01; calculation B03; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Strength: water and wastewater pumping adds a faster-growing, higher-margin segment. It supplies 24.06% of nine-month 2026 sales at a 17.70% operating margin and carried USD 325.0 million of backlog at the end of 2025, 11.2% above a year earlier. Basis: calculation B08; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10

Weakness: acquisitions outrun free cash flow and are funded with secured debt capacity. Free cash flow covered 58.52% of cash acquisitions from 2024 to nine months 2026, and acquired earnings are not disclosed, so the leverage effect of the deals cannot be tested. Basis: calculation B07; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94

Weakness: the debt is floating-rate, unhedged and concentrated in one maturity. A 100 bp rise costs about USD 8.4 million a year and USD 812.0 million falls due on 2030-10-13, 96.72% of principal. Basis: calculation B04; calculation B05; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14

Weakness: gross margin is falling while supplier terms are cancellable. The quarterly gross margin fell from 32.3% to 30.7% during 2026, and manufacturers can cancel distribution authorizations on little notice. Basis: calculation B09; 10-Q_2026-03-31_dxpe-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26

Weakness: financial policy and control cannot be verified. A USD 150.0 million buyback was authorized on 2026-10-28, equal to 142.91% of twelve-month free cash flow, and the proxy statement that would show the chief executive's holding and board independence is not supplied. Basis: calculation B10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The sources show no new notes or bonds in the period; DXP's two debt changes were bank-facility amendments. On 2025-12-16 the term loan agreement was amended to add USD 205.0 million of incremental commitments, leaving USD 848.0 million outstanding under it and moving some covenant compliance dates, and on 2026-07-02 the asset-based revolver was restated at up to USD 225.0 million, from USD 185.0 million, with a USD 50.0 million accordion and a 2031-07-02 maturity. The revolver was undrawn at 2026-09-30 and total debt was USD 839.5 million, all of it secured term loan. Basis: calculation A11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dxpe-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12

Acquisitions are the main transactions. Five businesses were bought in nine months 2026 for USD 153.6 million, of which 84.70% was cash, 14.34% contingent consideration and 0.97% shares, and all USD 76.4 million of the goodwill sits in Innovative Pumping Solutions. The annual report names three January and February 2026 purchases funded with cash on hand, Mequipco was bought on 2026-08-01 for cash and shares, and a purchase agreement for MDS of Michigan, LLC was signed on 2026-11-01 with cash on hand and no price stated. Basis: calculation A01; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dxpe-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

On 2026-10-28 the company entered into a program to buy back up to USD 150.0 million or 1.0 million shares over 24 months; no purchase is stated. The previous USD 85.0 million program ended in August 2026 with nothing bought in nine months 2026. Basis: calculation A08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: DXP ENTERPRISES INC (issuer id dxpe), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, transaction, ownership and operating-model facts, and the governance and shareholder-behavior assessment, drawn from the seven supplied filings and releases and the source-readiness answer. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery view is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplied module answer used by this module:

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: DXP is an acquisitive, listed industrial distributor with no sponsor or parent named in the sources, so creditors rely on management restraint: USD 153.6 million went on acquisitions in nine months 2026 and a USD 150.0 million buyback was authorized on 2026-10-28.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A01; calculation A08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating risk is moderate: no customer reaches 10% of sales, nine-month organic growth was 9.3%, and USD 411.0 million of liquidity sits against USD 839.5 million of debt. The view stays cautious because the chief executive's holding and the board's independence are not established and acquired earnings are not disclosed, so leverage after the deals cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A04; calculation A11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth is partly bought, which makes acquisition discipline the central credit variable. Sales rose 13.19% in nine months 2026 and organic sales rose 9.26%; acquired businesses supplied 8.27% of sales and 33.88% of Innovative Pumping Solutions sales in the third quarter, and 18 businesses cost USD 407.7 million across 2024, 2025 and nine months 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A03; calculation A04; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions outran free cash flow and were met from cash that the December 2025 term loan increase appears to have supplied. Free cash flow of USD 70.5 million covered 55.84% of the USD 126.2 million spent in nine months 2026 on acquisitions net of cash acquired, and the USD 205.0 million of new term loan commitments preceded the spending. The filings do not state what the loan proceeds were for, so this link is an analyst interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A02; calculation A08; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquired earnings are not disclosed, so the leverage effect of the acquisition program cannot be tested from the filings. The acquisition notes give consideration, goodwill, intangibles and sales but no acquired EBITDA, and management's covenant EBITDA of USD 270.0 million includes pro forma acquisition effects that the filings do not bridge; the company's 2.30x secured leverage rests on that figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 2; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns have been restrained so far, but the new authorization is large against free cash flow. Repurchases fell from USD 54.7 million in 2023 to USD 28.8 million in 2024, USD 17.0 million in 2025 and nothing in nine months 2026, and USD 68.0 million of the earlier authorization was left unused when that program ended in August 2026. The new USD 150.0 million program equals 142.91% of twelve-month free cash flow of USD 105.0 million and 68.55% of cash, and the term loan limits restricted payments with some baskets open only below stated leverage levels, but the basket sizes and thresholds are not supplied, so whether covenants would limit it is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A08; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control and governance cannot be verified because the proxy statement is not supplied. The chief executive has been Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer since 1996 and acquired a controlling interest in the predecessor company in 1986, but his current holding, the board's independence and its committee membership are not stated. Related-party dealings are small: USD 2.3 million of 2025 lease expense went to entities the chief executive and family control, 0.50% of selling, general and administrative expense, and the Audit Committee reviews related-party transactions above USD 120,000.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating risk is moderate and sits with suppliers and end markets, not customers. No customer reached 10% of sales in three years, over 90% of sales are products and 96.18% of 2025 sales were in the United States, but manufacturers can cancel distribution authorizations on little or no notice, part of revenue depends on oil, gas and petrochemical spending, and Supply Chain Services contracts can be cancelled on little or no notice. Backlog in Innovative Pumping Solutions was USD 325.0 million at the end of 2025, 11.2% above a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A06; calculation A12; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The group structure is simple and all outstanding debt is secured, but Canadian cash flows are outside the term loan guarantee. The issuer borrows the term loan, wholly owned material subsidiaries other than the Canadian ones guarantee it, and Canadian subsidiaries guarantee the revolver obligations of the Canadian borrowers but not the term loan; Canada was 3.35% of nine-month 2026 sales, so the gap is narrow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No creditor-adverse behavior is documented, though the record is incomplete. The sources show no dividend recapitalization, uptier, drop-down or non-pro-rata exchange, and the one term loan amendment of the period was agreed with lenders to add debt and adjust covenant dates. The annual report also says the company has at times been unable to meet covenants under earlier facilities and obtained waivers, without dates or detail.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is balance-sheet strength. Liquidity of USD 411.0 million is 48.47x the USD 8.5 million of scheduled principal due in each of 2027 to 2029, the company's own secured leverage of 2.30x is far below its maximum of 5.50x or 5.75x, S&P raised the rating to B+ in July 2026, no common dividend is paid, and total debt fell by USD 7.3 million in nine months 2026 even as acquisitions continued. Organic growth of 9.26% also shows the acquired businesses are not masking weak demand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A04; calculation A11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dxpe-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would soften if a proxy statement showed a majority-independent board and a modest insider holding, if acquired EBITDA and purchase multiples showed deals priced below current leverage, if the executed agreements showed restricted-payment baskets too small to take the USD 150.0 million program at current leverage, and if repurchases stayed inside free cash flow. It would harden if repurchases were paid from cash while acquisitions continued, if leverage rose without matching earnings, if a fall in acquisition sales exposed weaker organic growth, if a major manufacturer withdrew an authorization, or if the baskets proved large enough to fund the whole program while leverage stayed where it is.

fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so the chief executive's holding, the board's independence and any other large holder are not established; a large insider stake would raise key-person and related-party risk while an independent board would lessen it, so the governance conclusion could move either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquired EBITDA, purchase multiples and per-deal terms are not disclosed, so the conclusion on acquisition discipline rests on spending and sales contribution only; deals bought at high multiples or with weak margins would make it adverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreements are not supplied, so the size of restricted-payment, investment and incremental-debt baskets and the leverage levels that open them are unknown; the shareholder-return conclusion treats the USD 150.0 million program as unconstrained by anything quantified, and a tight basket would lessen the concern.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The use of the December 2025 term loan proceeds is not stated, so the link between that debt and the 2026 acquisitions is an interpretation; a different purpose would weaken the finding that growth is financed with secured debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - End-market and product-category shares appear in charts that the text does not carry and supplier concentration is not quantified, so the finding that risk sits with suppliers and end markets cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings name no sponsor, parent or fee arrangement, so the conclusion that no sponsor is present rests on silence; an undisclosed large holder with sponsor-like control would change the governance and shareholder-behavior conclusions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 quarterly reports give no segment backlog and no results for individual acquired businesses, so the operating conclusion for Innovative Pumping Solutions rests on reported sales and income only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sources show no new notes or bonds in the period; DXP's two debt changes were bank-facility amendments. On 2025-12-16 the term loan agreement was amended to add USD 205.0 million of incremental commitments, leaving USD 848.0 million outstanding under it and moving some covenant compliance dates, and on 2026-07-02 the asset-based revolver was restated at up to USD 225.0 million, from USD 185.0 million, with a USD 50.0 million accordion and a 2031-07-02 maturity. The revolver was undrawn at 2026-09-30 and total debt was USD 839.5 million, all of it secured term loan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions are the main transactions. Five businesses were bought in nine months 2026 for USD 153.6 million, of which 84.70% was cash, 14.34% contingent consideration and 0.97% shares, and all USD 76.4 million of the goodwill sits in Innovative Pumping Solutions. The annual report names three January and February 2026 purchases funded with cash on hand, Mequipco was bought on 2026-08-01 for cash and shares, and a purchase agreement for MDS of Michigan, LLC was signed on 2026-11-01 with cash on hand and no price stated.

fields.value: On 2026-10-28 the company entered into a program to buy back up to USD 150.0 million or 1.0 million shares over 24 months; no purchase is stated. The previous USD 85.0 million program ended in August 2026 with nothing bought in nine months 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by acquisition-led growth paid for with secured debt and by a control position that cannot be verified, because cash is committed to deals before their earnings are known and one executive's influence over acquisitions and buybacks is unchecked by disclosed board independence, which implies higher leverage and weaker creditor protection if deals underperform. Countervailing evidence is audited timely reporting, no common dividend, no buybacks in nine months 2026, USD 411.005 million of liquidity and no documented creditor-adverse transaction. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed agreements and acquired EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: DXP ENTERPRISES INC (issuer id dxpe), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the integrated fundamental credit view built from the seven supplied filings and releases and the three earlier module answers, covering business risk, financial profile, outlook, downside path and monitoring. No rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplied module answers used by this module:

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: DXP is an adequate fundamental credit whose main exposure is financial policy, not liquidity: broad customers, an 11.17% EBITDA margin and USD 411.0 million of liquidity protect debt service, while acquisitions and a new USD 150.0 million buyback could push floating-rate secured leverage up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B01; calculation B03; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage was 2.45x at 2026-09-30 and cash interest cover 4.20x, and pro forma net debt for the acquisition agreed on 2026-11-01 and for the new buyback is not established. The view rests on ownership, a covenant level and acquired earnings that the documents do not settle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B02; calculation B03; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are broad and growing, which is the main support for debt service. Twelve-month sales were USD 2,212.7 million, up 9.74% on FY2025, and reported EBITDA rose 13.07% to USD 247.2 million, lifting the margin from 10.84% to 11.17%; no customer reached 10% of sales and organic sales rose 9.26% in nine months 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B01; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate but has drifted up because growth is paid for with cash. Net debt rose 15.50% to USD 604.4 million while twelve-month EBITDA rose 13.07%, so net leverage moved from 2.39x at 2025-12-31 to 2.45x and total leverage is 3.33x; the company's own secured leverage of 2.30x is lower because it uses principal debt and covenant EBITDA of USD 270.0 million. These figures are before the acquisition agreed on 2026-11-01 and the new buyback; pro forma net debt and leverage are not established, because the price and any purchase are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B02; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt service is covered with room. Cash interest cover is 4.20x, liquidity is 48.47x the USD 8.5 million of principal due each year to 2029, and each 100 bp on the floating-rate term loan costs about USD 8.4 million, or 3.40% of EBITDA; with no hedges in place, a 200 bp rise would cut cover to 3.27x if the whole balance floats.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B03; calculation B04; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is concentrated in one year. USD 812.0 million, 96.72% of principal and 3.28x EBITDA, falls due on 2030-10-13, while the revolver now runs to 2031-07-02; S&P raised the rating to B+ in July 2026 and Moody's rated the corporate credit B1 at the end of 2025, but no market quotes are supplied, so pricing and market access are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B05; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is positive but flattered, so growth is not self-funded. Twelve-month free cash flow of USD 105.0 million compares with USD 54.0 million in FY2025 and benefits from cash taxes of USD 6.6 million against USD 35.1 million and capital expenditure of USD 10.2 million against USD 37.0 million in nine months; after USD 126.2 million of cash acquisitions the nine-month figure was negative USD 55.7 million, and free cash flow covered only 58.52% of cash acquisitions from 2024 to nine months 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B06; calculation B07; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross margin is the pressure point: it fell each quarter of 2026, from 32.3% to 31.8% to 30.7%, and the third quarter was 0.70 percentage points below a year earlier, which the company ties to higher input costs. Operating leverage hid this, because selling, general and administrative expense fell to 21.81% of third-quarter sales from 22.88%, but a further 100 bp of EBITDA margin loss would cost USD 22.1 million, 8.95% of EBITDA, and lift net leverage to 2.69x on unchanged net debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B09; 10-Q_2026-03-31_dxpe-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dxpe-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the swing factor for creditors. The company pays no common dividend and bought no shares in nine months 2026, but it authorized a USD 150.0 million buyback on 2026-10-28, equal to 142.91% of twelve-month free cash flow, while its chief executive's holding and the board's independence are not established; Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk as Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is moderate. Service Centers supply 64.23% of nine-month 2026 sales and depend on manufacturers who can cancel authorizations on little notice, part of revenue follows oil, gas and petrochemical spending, and tariffs and vendor price increases press on margin; against that, water and wastewater pumping now supplies 24.06% of sales at a 17.70% operating margin, with USD 325.0 million of backlog at the end of 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B08; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an adequate view is the structure of the debt, not today's ratios. Total leverage of 3.33x, floating-rate secured debt with no hedges, one USD 812.0 million maturity in 2030 and B-category agency ratings leave little room for error if earnings fall, and the twelve-month cash flow that supports coverage includes unusually low taxes and capital spending while acquisitions keep absorbing cash. If a 100 bp margin squeeze arrives as the quarterly gross margin trend suggests, net leverage would reach 2.69x before any buyback.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B02; calculation B04; calculation B05; calculation B06; calculation B09; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would strengthen if executed agreements confirmed a wide covenant cushion and baskets that limit the buyback, if acquired EBITDA showed the 2026 deals earning enough to lower leverage, and if gross margin recovered to its nine-month 2026 level of 31.58%. It would weaken if the buyback were paid from cash while acquisitions continued, if organic sales growth turned negative, if gross margin fell below the FY2024 level of 30.87%, or if the backlog in water and wastewater pumping fell below USD 325.0 million. Strength in liquidity of USD 411.0 million would still delay any liquidity event, so the weakening path is leverage and refinancing, not a near-term cash shortfall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B01; calculation B09; calculation B10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquired earnings and management guidance are not supplied, so the outlook and downside discussion rests on reported twelve-month figures and analyst sensitivities; deals that earn more than assumed would make the leverage view too cautious, and the reverse would make it too generous.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer, market-price or portfolio inputs are supplied, so the adequacy judgement is absolute rather than relative to comparable issuers, and market access is read from agency ratings alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Twelve-month figures are built from interim stubs that are unaudited, so a restated quarter would move the reported leverage and cover ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant level is stated differently in the annual and quarterly reports and no executed agreement is supplied, so the conclusion that covenants do not threaten liquidity rests on the company's stated ratio only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is absent, so the weight given to financial policy as the swing factor depends on a control position that cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No seasonal pattern or average-balance data is stated, so quarter-end liquidity may overstate or understate the cash cushion through the year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: customer breadth supports revenue durability. No customer reached 10% of sales in three years, over 90% of sales are products, and organic sales rose 9.26% in nine months 2026, so the earnings that service debt do not rest on one account or on acquisitions alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B01; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: liquidity and a light amortization profile remove near-term cash risk. Liquidity of USD 411.0 million is 48.47x the USD 8.5 million of principal due each year to 2029, and the revolver was extended to 2031-07-02.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B03; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: coverage and margin trajectory are favorable. Cash interest cover is 4.20x and the EBITDA margin rose from 10.84% in FY2025 to 11.17% over twelve months, helped by selling, general and administrative leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B01; calculation B03; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: water and wastewater pumping adds a faster-growing, higher-margin segment. It supplies 24.06% of nine-month 2026 sales at a 17.70% operating margin and carried USD 325.0 million of backlog at the end of 2025, 11.2% above a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B08; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: acquisitions outrun free cash flow and are funded with secured debt capacity. Free cash flow covered 58.52% of cash acquisitions from 2024 to nine months 2026, and acquired earnings are not disclosed, so the leverage effect of the deals cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B07; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: the debt is floating-rate, unhedged and concentrated in one maturity. A 100 bp rise costs about USD 8.4 million a year and USD 812.0 million falls due on 2030-10-13, 96.72% of principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B04; calculation B05; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: gross margin is falling while supplier terms are cancellable. The quarterly gross margin fell from 32.3% to 30.7% during 2026, and manufacturers can cancel distribution authorizations on little notice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B09; 10-Q_2026-03-31_dxpe-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: financial policy and control cannot be verified. A USD 150.0 million buyback was authorized on 2026-10-28, equal to 142.91% of twelve-month free cash flow, and the proxy statement that would show the chief executive's holding and board independence is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: DXP distributes maintenance, repair and operating products to industrial customers from a branch network in the United States and Canada, and also engineers custom pump packages and runs customers' procurement and storerooms. Service Centers supplied 68.10% of FY2025 sales, Innovative Pumping Solutions 19.36% and Supply Chain Services 12.54%, and sales grew from a business founded in 1908 to USD 2,016.4 million in FY2025 largely through acquisitions, 64 of them since 2004.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B08; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The model supports debt service because products are replacement and consumable items sold to a wide base, with no customer at 10% of sales, but it ties up working capital: receivables rose USD 52.6 million in nine months 2026. Cash flow is therefore durable in a stable economy and sensitive to industrial activity and to supplier terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B06; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: DXP is a listed Texas corporation with no sponsor or parent named in the documents. Its chairman, president and chief executive has led it since 1996 and acquired control of the predecessor company in 1986, but his current holding, the board's independence and the identity of the Series B preferred holders are not established; related-party leases are small at 0.50% of selling, general and administrative expense.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Material wholly owned subsidiaries other than the Canadian ones guarantee the term loan, and the U.S. ones guarantee the revolver, so Canada, at 3.35% of nine-month 2026 sales, sits outside the term loan guarantee. Leverage tolerance has been moderate, with net leverage between 2.39x and 2.45x, but acquisition appetite is high at USD 407.7 million across 18 businesses since 2024, and creditors' protection rests on covenants because no outside equity backstop is shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B02; calculation B07; calculation B10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is transactional and cyclical, not contracted. Customers buy on purchase orders, DXP traditionally has no long-term customer contracts, and the Supply Chain Services contracts that exist can be cancelled on little or no notice; demand follows industrial production, maintenance budgets and energy capital spending, so sales rose 11.89% in FY2025 and 13.19% in nine months 2026, of which 9.26% was organic.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B01; calculation B08; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is moderate. Management says it has kept strong margins despite vendor price increases, and the nine-month gross margin held at 31.58%, but the third quarter shows a lag: input costs cut the gross margin by 65 basis points. Backlog in Innovative Pumping Solutions of USD 325.0 million at the end of 2025 gives some visibility for that segment, though backlog can be delayed or cancelled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B09; calculation B08; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost of sales is 68.42% of nine-month 2026 sales, and after product cost labor is the largest expense. Selling, general and administrative expense of 22.65% of sales is mostly payroll, rent, insurance and professional fees, which are semi-fixed: they produced operating leverage in the third quarter, when the ratio fell to 21.81% from 22.88%, and they would work against margin if volumes fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B09; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure because capex and acquisitions are discretionary, but not fully against input-cost inflation or adverse mix: the quarterly gross margin fell from 32.3% to 30.7% during 2026, and a further 100 bp of EBITDA margin would cost USD 22.1 million, 8.95% of twelve-month EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B09; 10-Q_2026-03-31_dxpe-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dxpe-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low, at 2.00% of FY2025 sales and 0.60% in nine months 2026, and operating lease liabilities are USD 74.7 million, so most of EBITDA can convert to cash; free cash flow was 37.17% of nine-month EBITDA and 12.75% of carrying debt over twelve months. Conversion is flattered by cash taxes of USD 6.6 million in nine months 2026 against USD 35.1 million a year earlier, and working capital absorbed USD 41.9 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B06; calculation B09; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA translates into durable free cash flow for debt service and for some deleveraging, but not for both growth by acquisition and a large buyback at once: capex flexibility is high, yet acquisitions, contingent consideration of USD 30.7 million and the buyback all draw on the same cash, and no seasonal pattern is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B07; calculation B10; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high: the market is highly fragmented, DXP ranked 17th among U.S. distributors of these products, and several competitors have greater resources, so pricing is a constant constraint on margin and on the cash flow that services debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is moderate and the threat of substitutes comes mainly from manufacturers selling direct, which the company lists as a risk to sales and earnings; neither is shown to have hurt results, so the credit effect is a monitoring item.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is moderate: no customer is large, but customers can consolidate suppliers and DXP has few long-term contracts, which limits pricing. Supplier power is high, because manufacturers can cancel authorizations on little notice and set the prices that DXP must pass through, which is the main route to margin and availability risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two factors matter to credit. Economic conditions drive volumes and the cost of USD 839.5 million of floating-rate debt, and trade policy raises vendor costs: the company says new and expanded tariffs disrupt supply chains and that their effect cannot be predicted. Social and technological factors do not appear to be primary credit drivers on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B04; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are a broad customer base, liquidity of USD 411.0 million, an extended revolver and 4.20x cash interest cover, with a 9.26% organic growth record that does not depend on acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B01; calculation B03; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses are acquisition-funded growth that outruns free cash flow, floating-rate unhedged secured debt, one maturity in 2030, falling gross margin in 2026 and unverified control and covenant levels.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B04; calculation B05; calculation B07; calculation B09; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the full-year effect of the later 2026 acquisitions, growth in water and wastewater pumping where margin is highest, and use of free cash flow to cut leverage instead of buying back shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B08; calculation B10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats that could weaken it are a slowdown in industrial and energy activity, tariff-driven input cost inflation, a larger buyback or deal spending funded from cash, and a rise in rates on unhedged debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B04; calculation B09; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ranked strengths are customer breadth with organic growth, liquidity and a light amortization profile, coverage with a rising margin, and the water and wastewater platform. The ranked weaknesses are acquisition spending ahead of disclosed earnings, floating-rate debt with a single 2030 maturity, falling gross margin and supplier dependence, and unverified financial policy and control; each follows from the evidence and mechanism set out in Strengths and weaknesses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B01; calculation B03; calculation B05; calculation B07; calculation B08; calculation B09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are average: USD 2,212.7 million of twelve-month sales and a 17th ranking among U.S. distributors give shock-absorbing scale, and management calls DXP the largest North American distributor of rotating equipment, but there is no market-share data. Competitive advantage is average, resting on first-tier distribution, technical service and engineered pump packages, while authorizations are cancellable and no switching-cost data are supplied. Business diversification is average: customers and geography are broad, with 96.18% of FY2025 sales in the United States, but suppliers, end markets and the acquisition engine concentrate risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B01; calculation B08; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost and capex flexibility is strong, because capital expenditure is 0.60% to 2.00% of sales and acquisitions are discretionary, although selling, general and administrative expense is semi-fixed. Margin stability is average: the gross margin was 30.87% in FY2024, 31.54% in FY2025 and 31.58% in nine months 2026, with a 30.7% third quarter. Free cash flow stability is average: it was USD 77.1 million in FY2024, USD 54.0 million in FY2025 and USD 105.0 million over twelve months, moving with taxes, capital spending and working capital.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B06; calculation B07; calculation B09; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: the B+ and B1 ratings and a revolver to 2031 help, but 96.72% of principal matures in 2030 and no quotes are supplied. Liquidity is strong at USD 411.0 million. Financial policy and governance is average and could move to weak if the buyback proceeds from cash while deals continue, because ownership is unverified and the covenant level conflicts across documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B03; calculation B05; calculation B10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are customer breadth, liquidity and rising coverage; the main constraints are secured floating-rate leverage of 3.33x, acquisition-funded growth and a single 2030 maturity. The trend is steady in earnings, softer in gross margin and flat to slightly higher in net leverage, from 2.39x to 2.45x, and pro forma net debt for the acquisition agreed on 2026-11-01 and for the new buyback is not established. Missing datapoints are acquired EBITDA, the executed agreements, the proxy statement and peer data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B02; calculation B05; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months management expects to finish 2026 strongly with momentum into 2027 and, in the annual report, expected continued growth in 2026, but it gives no numeric guidance. Tailwinds are the full-year effect of the August 2026 Mequipco purchase and the agreed MDS of Michigan purchase, water and wastewater project demand, acquired businesses owned under twelve months that already added USD 48.8 million of sales in the third quarter, and operating leverage; headwinds are the 2026 fall in gross margin, tariff and input-cost inflation, a cash interest bill of USD 58.8 million over twelve months on unhedged debt, and the pull on cash from acquisitions and the buyback.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B03; calculation B09; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the term loan and revolver mature in 2030 and 2031, amortization is only 0.25% a quarter and the excess cash flow sweep, 50% falling to 25% below a Total Leverage Ratio of 3.00x and to nil at 2.50x or lower, adds little at current leverage, so deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth rather than repayment. The sector tailwind is infrastructure and water demand; the headwinds are industrial and energy cycles and tariff policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B05; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a slowdown in industrial production and energy capital spending while vendors raise prices faster than DXP can pass them on, which the third-quarter margin already hints at. The first operational break is gross margin and Service Centers volume, 64.23% of sales, with Innovative Pumping Solutions projects deferred or cancelled from the USD 325.0 million backlog.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B08; calculation B09; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial transmission is EBITDA: each 100 bp of margin lost costs USD 22.1 million, 8.95% of twelve-month EBITDA, and lifts net leverage from 2.45x to 2.69x on unchanged net debt, an Assumption-Based sensitivity and not a forecast; pro forma net debt for the acquisition agreed on 2026-11-01 and for the new buyback is not established. Falling receivables and inventory would release cash, but customer deposits and billings in excess of costs of USD 43.6 million would unwind, and cash interest would stay near USD 58.8 million because the debt is unhedged.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B02; calculation B03; calculation B09; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity of USD 411.0 million is 48.47x annual scheduled principal, the revolver fixed charge coverage test of 1.00x applies only in a compliance period triggered by low availability and stood at 2.98x, and the stated secured leverage of 2.30x is far below the stated maximum of 5.50x or 5.75x, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress. Management's levers are to stop acquisitions and the buyback, cut capital spending and release working capital; the stress falls on leverage and on the 2030 refinancing, where USD 812.0 million is 3.28x EBITDA today.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B03; calculation B05; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, DXP presents an adequate business profile supported by customer breadth, an 11.17% EBITDA margin and a growing water and wastewater platform, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition-led growth funded with secured debt, floating-rate debt with one 2030 maturity and financial policy that cannot be verified. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because capital intensity is low and twelve-month free cash flow was USD 105.0 million, tempered by working capital and acquisition draws. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA growth and market access in 2029 and 2030. The primary downside path is a gross margin squeeze from input costs in a softer industrial cycle while cash goes to acquisitions and buybacks. The business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers is not established because no peer data are supplied. Further analysis would require the proxy statement, the executed agreements, acquired EBITDA and peer data. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: leverage drift from acquisition and buyback spending.
